newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: FOCUS-Philippine H1 GNP growth seen at 6.4 pct.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Philippine H1 GNP growth seen at 6.4 pct.

text.p: A strong recovery in the domestic agriculture sector is expected to have bolstered the Philippines' economic growth in the first half of the year, economists and analysts said on Tuesday.

A Reuters survey of seven securities firms showed they were expecting 6.4 percent growth in Gross National Product (GNP) for the first six months of the year, higher than 5.2 percent growth posted in the same period last year.
The estimates ranged from a low of 6.0 to a high of 7.0 percent.
Brokers on the Philippine Stock Exchange, where prices were falling on Tuesday as the market took a breather from last week's steep run-up, said they expected the downward trend to fade.
The GNP figures are due to be released next week and expectations of higher growth were bound to fuel a rise in share prices, they said.

The agriculture sector, which had been the problem sector last year due to a series of typhoons and prolonged drought, was able to register 3.85 percent growth in the first half of the year, according to recent Agriculture Department Statistics.

"It's better than expected...Agriculture will definitely be one of the major sectors driving our economy higher towards the end of the year," said Noel Reyes, research head of Anscor-Hagedorn Securities.
The sector contracted by 0.69 percent in the second quarter last year, and posted measly 1.79 percent growth in the first quarter.
"The strong recovery in the agriculture sector is expected to sustain the growth momentum," Joey Cuyegkeng, an economist at ING Baring Securities, said.
Another factor cited as likely to accelerate growth was remittances from overseas.
Remittances rose by 58.7 percent in the first quarter of the year, and were expected to maintain their growth rate into the second quarter.
Raul Ruiz of Sun Hung Kai Securities said better job security among Filipino overseas workers had led to higher remittances.
Four million out of the 68 million Filipinos work abroad and their remittances are an important source of foreign exchange.
Among other indicators cited by analysts were strong manufacturing output, an active services sector, and rising purchasing power among consumers.
Indices measuring the value of production have been posting double-digit expansion in the first five months of the year, while power sales were up 10.6 percent in the first half.
Car sales, an indicator of rising purchasing power, grew by 26.6 percent in the first six months of the year.
Luz Lorenzo of Peregrine Securities added that building permit approvals were up by more than 20 percent.
However, Manuel Goseco of Dharmala Securities warned that rising import bills could put a brake on growth momentum. "The growing trade deficit is not that encouraging," he said.
Other analysts disagreed, saying that most of the imports are being used to produce more goods for export.
Analysts said with the present momentum, they expected full-year GNP to increase by 7.0 percent against 5.7 percent growth in 1995.
Following is the list of predictions:
BROKERAGE PREDICTION (PCT)
Anscor Hagedorn Securities - 6.5 to 6.9
BPI Capital Corp - 6.4
DBS Securities - 6.4 to 6.5
Dharmala Securities - 6.2
Peregrine Securities - 6.5 to 7.0
Philippine Asia Equity - 6.0 to 6.5
Sun Hung Kai Securities - 6.3
